key_insight: LingBot-Map introduces a feed-forward Geometric Context Transformer (GCT) that encodes geometric and temporal context from a video stream to produce accurate, temporally consistent 3D reconstructions in real time.
problem_solved: Enables streaming 3D reconstruction that balances geometric accuracy, temporal consistency, and computational efficiency for recovering camera poses and point clouds from continuous video.
method: Geometric Context Transformer (GCT): transformer blocks operate on geometric tokens (pose, depth, and feature embeddings) to fuse spatial and temporal context across frames.
Feed-forward SLAM-inspired pipeline: single-pass inference that predicts camera poses and incremental point-cloud updates without expensive iterative optimization.
Memory- and compute-efficient temporal aggregation: compact history representation and geometric-consistency losses/modules to maintain low latency and stable reconstructions.
impact: Provides a practical foundation model for real-time 3D perception that can be integrated into robotics, AR/VR, and autonomous systems, reducing reliance on heavy optimization-based SLAM while preserving geometric fidelity.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: video frames → GCT encoder → pose + point-cloud outputs, highlighting streaming (online) operation.
Architecture sketch: transformer with geometric tokens and temporal attention lanes.
Before/after reconstruction comparison: raw frames vs. reconstructed point cloud and camera trajectory to show temporal consistency.
Performance sketch: latency vs. reconstruction quality tradeoff (illustrative curve) to emphasize efficiency gains.
paper_title: Geometric Context Transformer for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Lin-Zhuo Chen, Jian Gao, Yihang Chen, Ka Leong Cheng, Yipengjing Sun
